# Stored data written by released builds

Each directory holds what one released build of the extension stored, so that
tests can load it with the current code. An update that drops, renames or
reshapes a stored field then fails a test instead of reaching users.

| File                                  | What it is                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<version>/chrome-storage-local.json` | `chrome.storage.local.get(null)` from the build's service worker profile            |
| `<version>/local-storage.json`        | The extension origin's `localStorage`                                               |
| `<version>/wallet.json`               | What the capture set up, as the build reported it through its own wallet controller |
| `release-storage.ts`                  | Reads the three files; `RELEASES` lists the captured versions                       |
| `capture/`                            | The Playwright run that produced them                                               |

They are read by:

- `packages/preference-service/test/release-storage.test.ts`
- `packages/contact-book/test/release-storage.test.ts`
- `packages/permission-service/test/release-storage.test.ts`
- `packages/keyring-service/test/release-storage.test.ts`
- `packages/wallet-state/test/release-storage.test.ts`
- `tests/e2e/scenarios/upgrade.spec.ts`

None of these files is part of the extension build or its ZIP.

## Test-only secrets

> **TEST ONLY. These seeds and this password are public. Never send funds to
> any address they derive, and never use them for a real wallet.**

Every wallet below was generated by the release itself during the capture,
used offline, and never held funds.

| Release | Password                      | Recovery phrase (24 words)                                                                                                                                               |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1.0.5   | `Qbit-Upgrade-Fixture-Only!1` | `federal wait thunder unhappy error dress obtain spike deposit ancient zone bacon proof truck sort ketchup matrix stable language cause price pen actor silent`          |
| 1.0.6   | `Qbit-Upgrade-Fixture-Only!1` | `climb lobster rain roast obey share school shock record garment pattern reopen day village jacket thought winter already kingdom priority crunch episode bone category` |
| 1.0.7   | `Qbit-Upgrade-Fixture-Only!1` | `final actress jazz mother one eagle educate put physical awake fence loud palace congress marriage high actual antique hint level above estate entire ranch`            |

The readonly wallets watch a secp256k1 public key generated for the capture;
its private key was never stored. The contact's address is the first testnet
account of the public test phrase `abandon` ×11 `about`.

## What each capture holds

The same steps ran on each build, from a fresh Chromium profile:

1. Create a wallet with the phrase the build generates and the password above.
2. Set auto-lock to 1 hour (the default 3 minutes would lock the wallet during
   the run) and switch to Qbit Testnet4.
3. Add a second account named `Savings`.
4. Turn on developer mode by tapping the version ten times in About.
5. Add a readonly wallet, which the build offers in developer mode.
6. Switch back to the mnemonic wallet and select `Savings`.
7. Add the contact `Fixture contact` on Testnet4.
8. Connect a loopback test page (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) through the
   build's own approval popup.
9. Choose the dark theme.
10. Collapse the balance card, hide balances, and type the contact's address
    and `0.0001` on the send screen without sending.
11. Switch the language to Español.

The browser resolves no host but `127.0.0.1`, so no explorer saw these wallets,
and the build's reads from them failed as they would offline. That is why
`phishing` and `phishing_list_fallback` are `null` and `notifications` is empty.
The `keyring_-1#0` account name is written in step 1. The create flow's
address-type screen previews the new wallet's address through a temporary
wallet (`createTmpKeyringWithMnemonics`), and the build stores a default name
for every account it shows, that one included. Step 7 derives the contact's
address the same way and finds the name already there.

Step 10 collapsed the balance card on 1.0.5 only. From 1.0.6 the card has no
breakdown to show, and ignores the click, until a balance loads, and offline
none does. The 1.0.6 and 1.0.7 captures therefore hold the default
`balanceDetailExpanded: true` in their saved `ui` state, and 1.0.5 holds
`false`. The capture checks the saved value either way, and records a step a
build could not take in `notes` in `wallet.json`. The three captures here
predate `notes`, so this paragraph records it for them.

Every captured `ui` state already holds `addressInput`, `amountInput` and the
other fields the wallet now fills in when it loads an older state
(`updateVersion` in `packages/wallet-state/src/reducers/ui.ts`). The one field
missing, `feeRateBar.feeRateSource` in 1.0.5 and 1.0.6, was filled in before
that change too. So these captures check that the fill keeps what the releases
saved, but they cannot show the `updateAddressInput` crash it prevents, which
needs a state without `addressInput`: the states built by hand in
`packages/wallet-state/test/reducers/ui.test.ts` show it.

| Release | ZIP                          | SHA-256                                                            | Captured   |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| 1.0.5   | `qbit-chrome-mv3-v1.0.5.zip` | `a209c86146c275d12ad9f25b82f9e8efe5941685a7241ed5943668d3c1e90cb4` | 2026-11-03 |
| 1.0.6   | `qbit-chrome-mv3-v1.0.6.zip` | `eef162762ab6b7ba04899da09dd6b209164d7cb96dfff315e5430d4110d4a30e` | 2026-11-03 |
| 1.0.7   | `qbit-chrome-mv3-v1.0.7.zip` | `7e36b57ae191a1738f370547c234f82070415d8dadac0a645b4f1b122855e748` | 2026-11-03 |

The ZIPs are the assets of the GitHub releases `v1.0.5`, `v1.0.6` and `v1.0.7`,
and the hashes match each release's `.sha256` asset. Each capture ran in Chrome
for Testing 149.0.7827.55 under Playwright 1.61.1, on Linux with Xvfb. Earlier
releases are not in this repository's history, so there are no captures of
them.

## Capture a release again

A capture creates a new wallet, so it rewrites every file of that release,
the recovery phrase included: update the table above with the one in the new
`wallet.json`.

```sh
TAG=v1.0.7
WORK=$(mktemp -d)
gh release download "$TAG" --repo Qbit-Org/qbit-wallet --dir "$WORK" \
  --pattern "qbit-chrome-mv3-$TAG.zip" --pattern "qbit-chrome-mv3-$TAG.zip.sha256"
(cd "$WORK" && sha256sum -c "qbit-chrome-mv3-$TAG.zip.sha256")
unzip -q "$WORK/qbit-chrome-mv3-$TAG.zip" -d "$WORK/extension"
mkdir "$WORK/profile"

# From the repository root. The second command installs Playwright's
# Chromium; to use another Chromium instead, skip it and set
# QBIT_E2E_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE to that browser's executable.
corepack pnpm install
corepack pnpm test:e2e:install-browser
QBIT_CAPTURE_RELEASE=$TAG \
QBIT_CAPTURE_EXTENSION_DIR="$WORK/extension" \
QBIT_CAPTURE_RELEASE_ZIP="$WORK/qbit-chrome-mv3-$TAG.zip" \
QBIT_CAPTURE_PROFILE_DIR="$WORK/profile" \
xvfb-run -a corepack pnpm exec playwright test \
  -c tests/fixtures/release-storage/capture/playwright.config.ts
```

The run writes `tests/fixtures/release-storage/<version>/`. Read any `notes` in
the new `wallet.json`, and say in this README what they mean for the data. It
refuses a profile directory that already holds a profile. A step can time out
on a busy host; run it again with a new, empty profile directory.

To add a release, capture it, add its version to `RELEASES` in
`release-storage.ts`, and add its row to the tables above. A later build may
need the capture's steps adjusted to its screens; keep the same wallet setup,
so that every release's data covers the same ground.
